 Sophie Devine has hit more sixes than any other player in WBBL history, but made a league-first call that proved the difference against the Thunder
 Sophie Devine has been hailed for her selflessness after making WBBL history on Thursday night, becoming the first player in the tournament to tactically retire out.
 The former New Zealand and Perth captain was on 42 from 39 deliveries when she left the field at the end of the 17th over, with the Scorchers batting first against a star-studded Sydney Thunder team at Drummoyne Oval.
 King and Mooney lead Scorchers to top of the table 
 Having struggled for rhythm and kept to 10 runs from the last 16 deliveries she faced, Devine voluntarily ended her innings.
 England allrounder Freya Kemp came out in her place and smashed 30 off 10, as the Scorchers added 47 runs from their final three overs.
 It proved the difference in a 17-run upset away win for the Scorchers, who are now undefeated after three games in Weber WBBL|12.
 Tactically retiring players who are not seen to be scoring quickly enough has become more common in T20 leagues, but it was the first time it had happened in the WBBL.
 Making it an even bigger call is the fact that Devine, one of the game's most decorated T20 players, has hit more sixes than anyone else in WBBL history and is generally renowned for her power hitting.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by Weber WBBL (@wbbl) 
 Speaking after the match, Scorchers captain Beth Mooney, who was out in the middle with Devine at the time, said it had been entirely the New Zealander's call.
 "Soph did a really selfless thing by retiring out," Mooney said on broadcast post-game. "She just thought she wasn't hitting it as clean, and Kempy came in.
 "I think once Soph's made her mind up about something, there's no arguing with her. We're all about doing the team thing at Scorchers.
 "I thought that was a good call from Soph, but when she's one of the best six-hitters in the world, it is tough to let her go.
 "Sometimes when you're batting, no matter how hard you're trying it just doesn't come off and Soph recognised that. As much as I was happy for her to stay out there ... Soph's always done the team thing and that showed tonight."
 There were three occasions where batters tactically retired out in the KFC BBL last summer: Nic Maddinson (Thunder), Muhammad Rizwan (Renegades) and Sam Harper (Stars).
 Maddinson became the first batter to be retired out in BBL history without an injury hampering him when he walked from the field on 30 off 26 against the Hurricanes. The move allowed Daniel Sams to come to the middle, with the latter duly hitting 16 off six deliveries as the Thunder posted a total of 205.
 Selfless act headlines Maddinson's Big Bash comeback 
 Rizwan meanwhile was called in by captain Will Sutherland after scoring 26 off 23 balls with the Renegades batting first against the Thunder.
 Harper then retired during a rain-reduced Knockout chase against the Hurricanes, walking off on 10 after struggling for fluency. It brought Glenn Maxwell to the middle and the move almost paid off, with the Stars falling three runs shy of their DLS target.
 Speaking on Channel Seven commentary on Thursday night, Trent Copeland and Katey Martin hailed the bravery of Devine's move as the match-defining difference.
 "This would have been (a target of) 165-170, Soph would have found a way to manufacture some boundaries but not 30 off 10 balls," Copeland said. "I think it was a masterstroke."
